# Pokedex — Checkpoint 02: PokéAPI data foundation

## Assignment
- Target agent: coding executor
- Mode: IMPLEMENTATION
- Boundary: CHECKPOINT
- Risk: LOW
- Repository: /home/thib/Documents/Lab/Pokedex
- Remote: ThibSama/Pokedex
- Branch: main
- Expected starting HEAD: fc6cf32fafa7d4c6f20adb8667fccae568fb70ce
- File authority: MODIFY_IN_SCOPE
- Command authority: RUN_TASK_SPECIFIC_RUNTIME_CHECKS
- Git authority: COMMIT_AND_PUSH_AFTER_REQUIRED_CHECKS
- Network authority: SPECIFIC_ALLOWLIST: pokeapi.co, docs.expo.dev, GitHub
- Secrets / external systems / metadata authority: NONE

## Verified starting state
Checkpoint 01 is accepted. Expo SDK 57 + Expo Router Stack are established; `/pokedex` is still a placeholder and `/pokemon/[id]` only echoes the route id. `AGENTS.md` requires current SDK docs for Expo APIs and lint + typecheck. AI traceability exists at `docs/ai-usage.jsonl` with `IMP-001`.

## Objective
Create the typed PokéAPI data foundation for National Dex #001–#251 and prove it by loading the first batch on the Pokédex screen. Keep API/raw data concerns outside route components.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Add clear typed domain models for a normalized Pokémon summary containing at least national `id`, canonical PokéAPI `apiName`, normal + shiny sprite URLs, and ordered type names.
2. Add a dedicated PokéAPI service. The supported scope is strictly National Dex IDs 1–251. Provide paginated/batched loading using `offset` + `limit`; default batch size 30. Never fetch all 251 detailed Pokémon eagerly.
3. The service normalizes PokéAPI responses and rejects/guards requests outside the supported range. UI components must not depend on large raw PokéAPI response shapes.
4. `/pokedex` uses `useState`/`useEffect` to load the first batch and has explicit loading, error, empty and success states.
5. Success rendering stays intentionally simple but visibly proves National Dex ordering: `#001`, `#002`, … with zero-padded IDs and names from the loaded data. Keep the temporary `/pokemon/197` navigation action available.
6. No search API or search implementation is introduced. Future search must filter only already-loaded client data.
7. Append `IMP-002` to `docs/ai-usage.jsonl` without altering `IMP-001`.

## Implementation requirements
Use the official PokéAPI v2 contract. Prefer small focused files such as `src/api/pokeApi.ts`, `src/types/pokemon.ts`, and constants only when useful. Use built-in `fetch`; add no data-fetching/state library. Preserve the existing Expo Router structure. Do not add speculative abstractions.

## Explicitly out of scope
Final Figma UI, reusable PokemonCard, pagination/infinite-scroll UI, search/sort/type filters, localized FR/EN names/species descriptions, detail-screen API integration, Showdown cries, favorites/collection persistence, shiny toggle UI, stat animation, dark mode, splash/icon, 3D.

## Preflight and safety
Read `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`; verify repo root, branch, exact HEAD, upstream and clean worktree. Inspect existing routes before editing. Stop on unexpected HEAD or unowned work. Do not reset/clean/stash unrelated changes.

## AI traceability
Append one valid JSONL object `IMP-002` containing timestamp, task, agent, exact received prompt verbatim, concise `response_summary`, meaningful accepted/modified/rejected `decisions` with reasons, and `changed_files`. Preserve previous lines byte-for-byte.

## Validation
Run:
- `npm run lint`
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npx expo export --platform android`
Perform one lightweight PokéAPI connectivity/shape check if useful. Do not add tests unless a concrete defect requires one.

## Git completion policy
Review the task-owned diff, stage only task-owned files, commit on `main`, push to `origin/main`. No force-push/rebase/history rewrite/PR mutation.

## Required final report
Status; starting-state verification; AC1–AC7 as PASS/FAIL/NOT PROVEN; files changed; exact checks/results; API/runtime evidence; final git status; commit SHA + push result; deferred work/risks.
response_summary: Verified HEAD fc6cf32 on main, clean worktree. Checked the live PokéAPI v2 /pokemon/{id} shape (id, name, sprites.front_default/front_shiny, sprites.other.official-artwork, types[].slot/type.name) and 404 behaviour before typing anything. Added src/types/pokemon.ts (PokemonSummary with id, apiName, sprites.normal/shiny, ordered types; PokemonBatch) and src/api/pokeApi.ts (constants for the 1–251 range and DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE=30; isSupportedDexId; fetchPokemonById with a RangeError guard before any network call and PokeApiError on non-OK responses; fetchPokemonBatch({offset, limit}) that derives the ID window from offset/limit, clamps to #251, fetches only that window via Promise.all and returns items/offset/limit/total/hasMore). Raw PokéAPI types are private to the service. Rewrote src/app/pokedex.tsx to load the first batch with useState/useEffect (cancel flag on unmount), with explicit loading, error (+ Retry), empty and success states; success renders a FlatList of "#001 bulbasaur grass / poison" rows with zero-padded IDs and keeps the temporary /pokemon/197 Link. No search code. Checks: npm run lint clean; npx tsc --noEmit clean; npx expo export --platform android succeeded. Runtime check of the service against pokeapi.co: first batch 30 items in order #1–#30 with hasMore=true; offset 240 returns 11 items ending at celebi with hasMore=false; #197 = umbreon with official-artwork normal/shiny URLs; IDs 0/252, offset 251 and limit 0 all reject with RangeError.

decisions.suggestion: Call /pokemon?offset&limit list endpoint first, then fetch each result URL
decisions.reason: IDs 1–251 are contiguous and known, so the list round-trip adds latency without information; deriving the ID window from offset/limit and fetching /pokemon/{id} directly still follows the official v2 contract.

decisions.suggestion: Use sprites.front_default / front_shiny as the summary sprite URLs
decisions.reason: Prefer sprites.other.official-artwork (higher resolution, suited to the future card UI) and fall back to front_default/front_shiny; typed as string | null because PokéAPI can return null.

decisions.suggestion: Return an empty batch for offsets past #251 instead of throwing
decisions.reason: AC3 asks the service to reject out-of-range requests; throwing RangeError makes a caller bug visible instead of silently ending pagination. In-range batches that overrun the end are clamped (offset 240 → 11 items).

decisions.suggestion: Reset to the loading state with setState at the top of the useEffect
decisions.reason: eslint react-hooks/set-state-in-effect rejects synchronous setState in effects; initial state is already loading and the Retry handler now sets loading before bumping the attempt counter.

decisions.suggestion: Add a generic useFetch/useAsync hook or a PokemonCard component
decisions.reason: Speculative abstraction; prompt requires plain useState/useEffect in the route and PokemonCard is out of scope.

decisions.suggestion: Add fetchPokemonById as a public export
decisions.reason: It is the unit fetchPokemonBatch is built from, carries the range guard, and is exactly what the detail screen will need next; no extra code was added for it.

decisions.suggestion: Add unit tests for the range guards
decisions.reason: No concrete defect; guards were exercised against the live API in a throwaway script (recorded in response_summary) instead.
